title: Chapter 4 – Jñāna-Karma-Sannyāsa Yoga (The Yoga of Knowledge and Renunciation of Action)
subtitle: Yoga of Renunciation of Action in Knowledge

verses.title: 4.1 imam vivasvate yogam
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
इमं विवस्वते योगं प्रोक्तवानहमव्ययम् ।
विवस्वान्मनवे प्राह मनुरिक्ष्वाकवेऽब्रवीत् ॥ ४-१॥
verses.roman:
śrībhagavānuvāca
imaṃ vivasvate yogaṃ proktavānahamavyayam
vivasvānmanave prāha manurikṣvākave'bravīt 4-1
verses.colloquial:
shriibhagavaan uvaacha
imam vivasvate yogam proktavaan aham avyayam
vivasvaan manave praaha manuh ikshvaakave 'braviit 4-1
verses.translation_reworded: The Blessed Lord said: I passed this imperishable Yoga on to Vivasvan. Vivasvan gave it to Manu, and Manu gave it to Ikshvaku.

verses.title: 4.2 evam parampara-praptam
verses.sanskrit:
एवं परम्पराप्राप्तमिमं राजर्षयो विदुः ।
स कालेनेह महता योगो नष्टः परन्तप ॥ ४-२॥
verses.roman:
evaṃ paramparāprāptamimaṃ rājarṣayo viduḥ
sa kāleneha mahatā yogo naṣṭaḥ parantapa 4-2
verses.colloquial:
evam paramparaa praaptam imam raajarshayo viduh
sa kaalena iha mahataa yogo nashtah parantapa 4-2
verses.translation_reworded: The royal sages received this knowledge, handed down from one to the next in an unbroken line. But over a long stretch of time, O Parantapa (burner of the foes), this Yoga has been lost in the world.

verses.title: 4.3 sa evayam maya te
verses.sanskrit:
स एवायं मया तेऽद्य योगः प्रोक्तः पुरातनः ।
भक्तोऽसि मे सखा चेति रहस्यं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥ ४-३॥
verses.roman:
sa evāyaṃ mayā te'dya yogaḥ proktaḥ purātanaḥ
bhakto'si me sakhā ceti rahasyaṃ hyetaduttamam 4-3
verses.colloquial:
sa evaayam mayaa te'dya yogah proktah puraatanah
bhakto'si me sakhaa cheti rahasyam hy etad uttamam 4-3
verses.translation_reworded: Today I have taught you that very same ancient Yoga, because you are My devotee and My friend. It is the highest secret.

verses.title: 4.4 aparam bhavato janma
verses.sanskrit:
अर्जुन उवाच ।
अपरं भवतो जन्म परं जन्म विवस्वतः ।
कथमेतद्विजानीयां त्वमादौ प्रोक्तवानिति ॥ ४-४॥
verses.roman:
arjuna uvāca
aparaṃ bhavato janma paraṃ janma vivasvataḥ
kathametadvijānīyāṃ tvamādau proktavāniti 4-4
verses.colloquial:
arjuna uvaacha
aparam bhavato janma param janma vivasvatah
katham etad vijaaniiyaam tvam aadau proktavaan iti 4-4
verses.translation_reworded: Arjuna said: You were born recently, while Vivaswan (the Sun) was born long before. How, then, am I to understand that You taught this Yoga at the beginning?

verses.title: 4.5 bahuni me vyatitani
verses.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ।
बहूनि मे व्यतीतानि जन्मानि तव चार्जुन ।
तान्यहं वेद सर्वाणि न त्वं वेत्थ परन्तप ॥ ४-५॥
verses.roman:
śrībhagavānuvāca
bahūni me vyatītāni janmāni tava cārjuna
tānyahaṃ veda sarvāṇi na tvaṃ vettha parantapa 4-5
verses.colloquial:
shrii bhagavaan uvaacha
bahuuni me vyatiitaani janmaani tava cha arjuna
taani aham veda sarvaani na tvam vettha parantapa 4-5
verses.translation_reworded: The Blessed Lord said: I have gone through many births, Arjuna, and so have you. I remember them all; you do not, O Parantapa (scorcher of foes).

verses.title: 4.6 ajo pi sannavyayatma
verses.sanskrit:
अजोऽपि सन्नव्ययात्मा भूतानामीश्वरोऽपि सन् ।
प्रकृतिं स्वामधिष्ठाय सम्भवाम्यात्ममायया ॥ ४-६॥
verses.roman:
ajo'pi sannavyayātmā bhūtānāmīśvaro'pi san
prakṛtiṃ svāmadhiṣṭhāya sambhavāmyātmamāyayā 4-6
verses.colloquial:
ajo'pi san avyayaatmaa bhuutaanaam iishvaro'pi san
prakritim svaam adhishthaaya sambhavaami aatma maayayaa 4-6
verses.translation_reworded: Although I am unborn and My nature never perishes, and although I am the Lord of all beings, I still take birth through My own Maya, keeping My own Nature under My command.

verses.title: 4.7 yada yada hi dharmasya
verses.sanskrit:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत ।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम् ॥ ४-७॥
verses.roman:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānirbhavati bhārata
abhyutthānamadharmasya tadātmānaṃ sṛjāmyaham 4-7
verses.colloquial:
yadaa yadaa hi dharmasya glaanirbhavati bhaarata
abhyutthaanam adharmasya tadaatmaanam srijaami aham 4-7
verses.translation_reworded: Whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness gains ground, O Bharata, I bring Myself into manifestation.

verses.title: 4.8 paritranaya sadhunam
verses.sanskrit:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् ।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे ॥ ४-८॥
verses.roman:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṃ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām
dharmasaṃsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge 4-8
verses.colloquial:
paritraanaaya saadhuunaam vinaashaaya cha dushkritaam
dharma samsthaapana arthaaya sambhavaami yuge yuge 4-8
verses.translation_reworded: Age after age I am born to protect the good, to destroy the wicked, and to set righteousness firmly in place.

verses.title: 4.9 janma karma cha me
verses.sanskrit:
जन्म कर्म च मे दिव्यमेवं यो वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
त्यक्त्वा देहं पुनर्जन्म नैति मामेति सोऽर्जुन ॥ ४-९॥
verses.roman:
janma karma ca me divyamevaṃ yo vetti tattvataḥ
tyaktvā dehaṃ punarjanma naiti māmeti so'rjuna 4-9
verses.colloquial:
janma karma cha me divyam evam yo vetti tattvatah
tyaktvaa deham punar janma naiti maam eti so 'rjuna 4-9
verses.translation_reworded: Whoever truly understands My divine birth and My divine action is not born again after leaving the body. That person comes to Me, Arjuna.

verses.title: 4.10 vita-raga-bhaya-krodha
verses.sanskrit:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।
बहवो ज्ञानतपसा पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥ ४-१०॥
verses.roman:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ
bahavo jñānatapasā pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ 4-10
verses.colloquial:
viita raaga bhaya krodhaa manmayaa maam upaashritaah
bahavo jnaana tapasaa puutaa mad bhaavam aagataah 4-10
verses.translation_reworded: Many, released from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in Me and sheltering in Me, have been purified by the Fire of Knowledge and have reached My Being.

verses.title: 4.11 ye yatha mam prapadyante
verses.sanskrit:
ये यथा मां प्रपद्यन्ते तांस्तथैव भजाम्यहम् ।
मम वर्त्मानुवर्तन्ते मनुष्याः पार्थ सर्वशः ॥ ४-११॥
verses.roman:
ye yathā māṃ prapadyante tāṃstathaiva bhajāmyaham
mama vartmānuvartante manuṣyāḥ pārtha sarvaśaḥ 4-11
verses.colloquial:
ye yathaa maam prapadyante taams tathaiva bhajaami aham
mama vartma anuvartante manushyaah paartha sarvashah 4-11
verses.translation_reworded: However people come to Me, that is how I reward them. In every way they walk, O son of Pritha, it is My path they are treading.

verses.title: 4.12 kankshantah karmanam
verses.sanskrit:
काङ्क्षन्तः कर्मणां सिद्धिं यजन्त इह देवताः ।
क्षिप्रं हि मानुषे लोके सिद्धिर्भवति कर्मजा ॥ ४-१२॥
verses.roman:
kāṅkṣantaḥ karmaṇāṃ siddhiṃ yajanta iha devatāḥ
kṣipraṃ hi mānuṣe loke siddhirbhavati karmajā 4-12
verses.colloquial:
kaankshantah karmanaam siddhim yajanta iha devataah
kshipram hi maanushe loke siddhir bhavati karma jaa 4-12
verses.translation_reworded: Those who want their actions in this world to bear fruit offer sacrifices to the gods, because results from action come quickly in the world of objects.

verses.title: 4.13 chatur-varnyam maya
verses.sanskrit:
चातुर्वर्ण्यं मया सृष्टं गुणकर्मविभागशः ।
तस्य कर्तारमपि मां विद्ध्यकर्तारमव्ययम् ॥ ४-१३॥
verses.roman:
cāturvarṇyaṃ mayā sṛṣṭaṃ guṇakarmavibhāgaśaḥ
tasya kartāramapi māṃ viddhyakartāramavyayam 4-13
verses.colloquial:
chaatur varnyam mayaa srishtam guna karma vibhaagashah
tasya kartaaram api maam viddhi akartaaram avyayam 4-13
verses.translation_reworded: I created the four castes according to the division of guna and karma. Yet although I am their author, know Me as the one who does nothing and never changes.

verses.title: 4.14 na mam karmani limpanti
verses.sanskrit:
न मां कर्माणि लिम्पन्ति न मे कर्मफले स्पृहा ।
इति मां योऽभिजानाति कर्मभिर्न स बध्यते ॥ ४-१४॥
verses.roman:
na māṃ karmāṇi limpanti na me karmaphale spṛhā
iti māṃ yo'bhijānāti karmabhirna sa badhyate 4-14
verses.colloquial:
na maam karmaani limpanti na me karma phale sprihaa
iti maam yo'bhijaanaati karmabhir na sa badhyate 4-14
verses.translation_reworded: Actions leave no stain on Me, and I have no craving for the fruits of action. Whoever knows Me in this way is not bound by what he does.

verses.title: 4.15 evam jnatva kritam
verses.sanskrit:
एवं ज्ञात्वा कृतं कर्म पूर्वैरपि मुमुक्षुभिः ।
कुरु कर्मैव तस्मात्त्वं पूर्वैः पूर्वतरं कृतम् ॥ ४-१५॥
verses.roman:
evaṃ jñātvā kṛtaṃ karma pūrvairapi mumukṣubhiḥ
kuru karmaiva tasmāttvaṃ pūrvaiḥ pūrvataraṃ kṛtam 4-15
verses.colloquial:
evam jnaatvaa kritam karma puurvair api mumukshubhih
kuru karmaiva tasmaat tvam puurvaih puurva taram kritam 4-15
verses.translation_reworded: Knowing this, the seekers of freedom in ancient times still performed action. So you too should act, as those of old did long ago.

verses.title: 4.16 kim karma kim akarmeti
verses.sanskrit:
किं कर्म किमकर्मेति कवयोऽप्यत्र मोहिताः ।
तत्ते कर्म प्रवक्ष्यामि यज्ज्ञात्वा मोक्ष्यसेऽशुभात् ॥ ४-१६॥
verses.roman:
kiṃ karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitāḥ
tatte karma pravakṣyāmi yajjñātvā mokṣyase'śubhāt 4-16
verses.colloquial:
kim karma kimakarmeti kavayo'pyatra mohitaah
tat te karma pravakshyaami yat jnaatvaa mokshyase ashubhaat 4-16
verses.translation_reworded: What is action? What is inaction? Even the wise are confused about this. So I will explain to you what action is (the nature of action and inaction), and by understanding it you will be freed from evil (from samsara, the wheel of birth and death).

verses.title: 4.17 karmano hyapi boddhavyam
verses.sanskrit:
कर्मणो ह्यपि बोद्धव्यं बोद्धव्यं च विकर्मणः ।
अकर्मणश्च बोद्धव्यं गहना कर्मणो गतिः ॥ ४-१७॥
verses.roman:
karmaṇo hyapi boddhavyaṃ boddhavyaṃ ca vikarmaṇaḥ
akarmaṇaśca boddhavyaṃ gahanā karmaṇo gatiḥ 4-17
verses.colloquial:
karmano hyapi boddhavyam boddhavyam cha vikarmanah
akarmanashcha boddhavyam gahanaa karmano gatih 4-17
verses.translation_reworded: One truly needs to understand (the real nature of) right action, and also of forbidden (or unlawful) action and of inaction. The nature (the path) of action is hard to fathom.

verses.title: 4.18 karmanyakarma yah
verses.sanskrit:
कर्मण्यकर्म यः पश्येदकर्मणि च कर्म यः ।
स बुद्धिमान्मनुष्येषु स युक्तः कृत्स्नकर्मकृत् ॥ ४-१८॥
verses.roman:
karmaṇyakarma yaḥ paśyedakarmaṇi ca karma yaḥ
sa buddhimānmanuṣyeṣu sa yuktaḥ kṛtsnakarmakṛt 4-18
verses.colloquial:
karmani akarma yah pashyet akarmani cha karma yah
sa buddhimaan manushyeshu sa yuktah kritsna karma krit 4-18
verses.translation_reworded: Whoever sees inaction within action and action within inaction is wise among people. Such a one is a yogi and has truly accomplished all action.

verses.title: 4.19 yasya sarve samarambhah
verses.sanskrit:
यस्य सर्वे समारम्भाः कामसङ्कल्पवर्जिताः ।
ज्ञानाग्निदग्धकर्माणं तमाहुः पण्डितं बुधाः ॥ ४-१९॥
verses.roman:
yasya sarve samārambhāḥ kāmasaṅkalpavarjitāḥ
jñānāgnidagdhakarmāṇaṃ tamāhuḥ paṇḍitaṃ budhāḥ 4-19
verses.colloquial:
yasya sarve samaarambhaah kaama sankalpa varjitaah
jnaana agni dagdha karmaanam tam aahuh panditam budhaah 4-19
verses.translation_reworded: When all of a person's undertakings are free of desire and personal purpose, and his actions have been burned away by the Fire of Knowledge, the wise call him a Sage.

verses.title: 4.20 tyaktva karma-phalasangam
verses.sanskrit:
त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः ।
कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥ ४-२०॥
verses.roman:
tyaktvā karmaphalāsaṅgaṃ nityatṛpto nirāśrayaḥ
karmaṇyabhipravṛtto'pi naiva kiñcitkaroti saḥ 4-20
verses.colloquial:
tyaktvaa karma phala aasangam nitya triptah niraashrayah
karmani abhipravrittah api na eva kinchit karoti sah 4-20
verses.translation_reworded: Having let go of attachment to the fruits of action, always content and relying on nothing, he does nothing at all even while he is busy acting.

verses.title: 4.21 nirashir yata-chittatma
verses.sanskrit:
निराशीर्यतचित्तात्मा त्यक्तसर्वपरिग्रहः ।
शारीरं केवलं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥ ४-२१॥
verses.roman:
nirāśīryatacittātmā tyaktasarvaparigrahaḥ
śārīraṃ kevalaṃ karma kurvannāpnoti kilbiṣam 4-21
verses.colloquial:
niraashiir yata chitta aatmaa tyakta sarva parigrahah
shaariiram kevalam karma kurvan na aapnoti kilbisham 4-21
verses.translation_reworded: Free of expectation, with mind and self under control, having given up every possession, performing action with the body alone, he commits no sin.

verses.title: 4.22 yadrichchha-labha-santushto
verses.sanskrit:
यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः ।
समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥ ४-२२॥
verses.roman:
yadṛcchālābhasantuṣṭo dvandvātīto vimatsaraḥ
samaḥ siddhāvasiddhau ca kṛtvāpi na nibadhyate 4-22
verses.colloquial:
yadricchaa laabha santushto dvandva atiitah vimatsarah
samah siddhaa avasiddhau cha kritvaa api na nibadhyate 4-22
verses.translation_reworded: Satisfied with whatever comes without effort, beyond the pairs of opposites and free of envy, steady alike in success and failure, he acts but is not bound.

verses.title: 4.23 gata-sangasya muktasya
verses.sanskrit:
गतसङ्गस्य मुक्तस्य ज्ञानावस्थितचेतसः ।
यज्ञायाचरतः कर्म समग्रं प्रविलीयते ॥ ४-२३॥
verses.roman:
gatasaṅgasya muktasya jñānāvasthitacetasaḥ
yajñāyācarataḥ karma samagraṃ pravilīyate 4-23
verses.colloquial:
gata sangasya muktasya jnaana avasthita chetasah
yajnaaya aacharatah karma samagram praviliiyate 4-23
verses.translation_reworded: For one who is without attachment, who is liberated, whose mind rests in knowledge, and who acts only as a sacrifice, every action dissolves completely.

verses.title: 4.24 brahmarpanam brahma
verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम् ।
ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना ॥ ४-२४॥
verses.roman:
brahmārpaṇaṃ brahma havirbrahmāgnau brahmaṇā hutam
brahmaiva tena gantavyaṃ brahmakarmasamādhinā 4-24
verses.colloquial:
brahma arpanam brahma havir brahmaagnau brahmanaa hutam
brahmaiva tena gantavyam brahma karma samaadhinaa 4-24
verses.translation_reworded: Brahman is the offering; Brahman is the clarified butter and the rest that make up the oblation; Brahman pours the offering into the fire that is Brahman. One who sees Brahman in every action will surely reach Brahman.

verses.title: 4.25 daivam evapare yajnam
verses.sanskrit:
दैवमेवापरे यज्ञं योगिनः पर्युपासते ।
ब्रह्माग्नावपरे यज्ञं यज्ञेनैवोपजुह्वति ॥ ४-२५॥
verses.roman:
daivamevāpare yajñaṃ yoginaḥ paryupāsate
brahmāgnāvapare yajñaṃ yajñenaivopajuhvati 4-25
verses.colloquial:
daivam eva apare yajnam yoginah paryupaasate
brahmaagnau apare yajnam yajnena eva upajuhvati 4-25
verses.translation_reworded: Some yogis offer sacrifice only to the devas (deva-yajna). Others offer the sacrifice itself as a sacrifice, through the Self, into the Fire of Brahman (brahma-yajna).

verses.title: 4.26 shrotradinindriyanyanye
verses.sanskrit:
श्रोत्रादीनीन्द्रियाण्यन्ये संयमाग्निषु जुह्वति ।
शब्दादीन्विषयानन्य इन्द्रियाग्निषु जुह्वति ॥ ४-२६॥
verses.roman:
śrotrādīnīndriyāṇyanye saṃyamāgniṣu juhvati
śabdādīnviṣayānanya indriyāgniṣu juhvati 4-26
verses.colloquial:
shrotraadiini indriyaany anye samyama agnishu juhvati
shabdaadiin vishayaan anya indriya agnishu juhvati 4-26
verses.translation_reworded: Some offer hearing and the other senses into the fires of restraint. Others offer sound and the other sense objects into the fires of the senses.

verses.title: 4.27 sarvanindriya-karmani
verses.sanskrit:
सर्वाणीन्द्रियकर्माणि प्राणकर्माणि चापरे ।
आत्मसंयमयोगाग्नौ जुह्वति ज्ञानदीपिते ॥ ४-२७॥
verses.roman:
sarvāṇīndriyakarmāṇi prāṇakarmāṇi cāpare
ātmasaṃyamayogāgnau juhvati jñānadīpite 4-27
verses.colloquial:
sarvaani indriya karmaani praana karmaani cha apare
aatma samyama yoga agnau juhvati jnaana diipite 4-27
verses.translation_reworded: Still others offer every function of the senses and every function of the breath (vital energy) into the fire of the Yoga of self-restraint, a fire lit by knowledge.

verses.title: 4.28 dravya-yajnas tapo-yajna
verses.sanskrit:
द्रव्ययज्ञास्तपोयज्ञा योगयज्ञास्तथापरे ।
स्वाध्यायज्ञानयज्ञाश्च यतयः संशितव्रताः ॥ ४-२८॥
verses.roman:
dravyayajñāstapoyajñā yogayajñāstathāpare
svādhyāyajñānayajñāśca yatayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ 4-28
verses.colloquial:
dravya yajnaah tapo yajnaa yoga yajnaah tathaa apare
svaadhyaaya jnaana yajnaah cha yatayah samshita vrataah 4-28
verses.translation_reworded: Others offer wealth, austerity, and Yoga as their sacrifice, while ascetics of firm vows and self-discipline offer scriptural study and knowledge as theirs.

verses.title: 4.29 apane juhvati pranam
verses.sanskrit:
अपाने जुह्वति प्राणं प्राणेऽपानं तथापरे ।
प्राणापानगती रुद्ध्वा प्राणायामपरायणाः ॥ ४-२९॥
verses.roman:
apāne juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe'pānaṃ tathāpare
prāṇāpānagatī ruddhvā prāṇāyāmaparāyaṇāḥ 4-29
verses.colloquial:
apaane juhvati praanam praane 'paanam tathaapare
praana apaana gatii ruddhvaa praanaayaama paraayanaah 4-29
verses.translation_reworded: Others, intent solely on breath control, offer the outgoing breath into the incoming and the incoming into the outgoing, holding back the flow of both.

verses.title: 4.30 apare niyataharah
verses.sanskrit:
अपरे नियताहाराः प्राणान्प्राणेषु जुह्वति ।
सर्वेऽप्येते यज्ञविदो यज्ञक्षपितकल्मषाः ॥ ४-३०॥
verses.roman:
apare niyatāhārāḥ prāṇānprāṇeṣu juhvati
sarve'pyete yajñavido yajñakṣapitakalmaṣāḥ 4-30
verses.colloquial:
apare niyataahaaraah praanaan praaneshu juhvati
sarve'pi ete yajna vidah yajna kshapita kalmashaah 4-30
verses.translation_reworded: Others, keeping their diet carefully regulated, offer the vital airs into the Vital Air. All of these understand sacrifice, and sacrifice has destroyed their sins.

verses.title: 4.31 yajna-shishtamrita-bhujo
verses.sanskrit:
यज्ञशिष्टामृतभुजो यान्ति ब्रह्म सनातनम् ।
नायं लोकोऽस्त्ययज्ञस्य कुतोऽन्यः कुरुसत्तम ॥ ४-३१॥
verses.roman:
yajñaśiṣṭāmṛtabhujo yānti brahma sanātanam
nāyaṃ loko'styayajñasya kuto'nyaḥ kurusattama 4-31
verses.colloquial:
yajna shishta amrita bhujo yaanti brahma sanaatanam
naayam loko'styayajnasya kuto'nyah kuru sattama 4-31
verses.translation_reworded: Those who eat the nectar that remains after the sacrifice go to the eternal Brahman. For one who performs no sacrifice, not even this world is his; how then could the other (world) be, O best of the Kurus?

verses.title: 4.32 evam bahu-vidha yajna
verses.sanskrit:
एवं बहुविधा यज्ञा वितता ब्रह्मणो मुखे ।
कर्मजान्विद्धि तान्सर्वानेवं ज्ञात्वा विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ ४-३२॥
verses.roman:
evaṃ bahuvidhā yajñā vitatā brahmaṇo mukhe
karmajānviddhi tānsarvānevaṃ jñātvā vimokṣyase 4-32
verses.colloquial:
evam bahuvidhaa yajnaa vitataa brahmano mukhe
karma jaan viddhi taan sarvaan evam jnaatvaa vimokshyase 4-32
verses.translation_reworded: In this way sacrifices of many kinds are laid out before Brahman (literally, at the mouth or face of Brahman). Know that all of them arise from action, and with that knowledge you will be set free.

verses.title: 4.33 shreyan dravya-mayad
verses.sanskrit:
श्रेयान्द्रव्यमयाद्यज्ञाज्ज्ञानयज्ञः परन्तप ।
सर्वं कर्माखिलं पार्थ ज्ञाने परिसमाप्यते ॥ ४-३३॥
verses.roman:
śreyāndravyamayādyajñājjñānayajñaḥ parantapa
sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārtha jñāne parisamāpyate 4-33
verses.colloquial:
shreyaan dravyamayaad yajnaaj jnaanayajnah parantapa
sarvam karma akhilam paartha jnaane parisamaapyate 4-33
verses.translation_reworded: The sacrifice of knowledge is greater than sacrifice with material objects, O Parantapa. Every action without exception, O Partha, comes to its fulfillment in Knowledge.

verses.title: 4.34 tad viddhi pranipatena
verses.sanskrit:
तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया ।
उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥ ४-३४॥
verses.roman:
tadviddhi praṇipātena paripraśnena sevayā
upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ 4-34
verses.colloquial:
tadviddhi pranipaatena pariprashnena sevayaa
upadekshyanti te jnaanam jnaaninas tattvadarshinah 4-34
verses.translation_reworded: Understand that the wise who have realized the Truth will teach you (that) Knowledge when you approach them with deep prostration, with questions, and with service.

verses.title: 4.35 yaj jnatva na punar
verses.sanskrit:
यज्ज्ञात्वा न पुनर्मोहमेवं यास्यसि पाण्डव ।
येन भूतान्यशेषेण द्रक्ष्यस्यात्मन्यथो मयि ॥ ४-३५॥ var अशेषाणि
verses.roman:
yajjñātvā na punarmohamevaṃ yāsyasi pāṇḍava
yena bhūtānyaśeṣeṇa drakṣyasyātmanyatho mayi 4-35
verses.colloquial:
yaj jnaatvaa na punar moham evam yaasyasi paandava
yena bhuutaani asheshena drakshyasi aatmani atho mayi 4-35
verses.translation_reworded: Once you know it, O Pandava, you will never again fall into delusion like this. Through it you will see all beings in your own Self, and in Me as well.

verses.title: 4.36 api ched asi papebhyah
verses.sanskrit:
अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः ।
सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥ ४-३६॥
verses.roman:
api cedasi pāpebhyaḥ sarvebhyaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ
sarvaṃ jñānaplavenaiva vṛjinaṃ santariṣyasi 4-36
verses.colloquial:
api chedasi paapebhyah sarvebhyah paapakrittamah
sarvam jnaana plavenaiva vrijinam santarishyasi 4-36
verses.translation_reworded: Even if you were the worst sinner of all, you would still cross beyond every sin on the raft of Knowledge.

verses.title: 4.37 yathaidhansi samiddho
verses.sanskrit:
यथैधांसि समिद्धोऽग्निर्भस्मसात्कुरुतेऽर्जुन ।
ज्ञानाग्निः सर्वकर्माणि भस्मसात्कुरुते तथा ॥ ४-३७॥
verses.roman:
yathaidhāṃsi samiddho'gnirbhasmasātkurute'rjuna
jñānāgniḥ sarvakarmāṇi bhasmasātkurute tathā 4-37
verses.colloquial:
yathaa edhaamsi samiddhah agnih bhasmasaat kurute arjuna
jnaana agnih sarva karmaani bhasmasaat kurute tathaa 4-37
verses.translation_reworded: Just as a blazing fire turns fuel to ashes, Arjuna, so the Fire of Knowledge turns all actions to ashes.

verses.title: 4.38 na hi jnanena sadrisham
verses.sanskrit:
न हि ज्ञानेन सदृशं पवित्रमिह विद्यते ।
तत्स्वयं योगसंसिद्धः कालेनात्मनि विन्दति ॥ ४-३८॥
verses.roman:
na hi jñānena sadṛśaṃ pavitramiha vidyate
tatsvayaṃ yogasaṃsiddhaḥ kālenātmani vindati 4-38
verses.colloquial:
na hi jnaanena sadrisham pavitram iha vidyate
tat svayam yoga samsiddhah kaalena aatmani vindati 4-38
verses.translation_reworded: Nothing in this world purifies as Knowledge does. One who has become perfect in Yoga discovers it in the Self, in due time.

verses.title: 4.39 shraddhavanllabhate
verses.sanskrit:
श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः ।
ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥ ४-३९॥
verses.roman:
śraddhāvām̐llabhate jñānaṃ tatparaḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ
jñānaṃ labdhvā parāṃ śāntimacireṇādhigacchati 4-39
verses.colloquial:
shraddhaavaam labhate jnaanam tatparah samyata indriyah
jnaanam labdhvaa paraam shaantim achirena adhigacchati 4-39
verses.translation_reworded: A person full of faith, devoted to It, with the senses mastered, gains (this) Knowledge. Having gained it, he soon reaches the Supreme Peace.

verses.title: 4.40 ajnash chashraddadhanash
verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञश्चाश्रद्दधानश्च संशयात्मा विनश्यति ।
नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न सुखं संशयात्मनः ॥ ४-४०॥
verses.roman:
ajñaścāśraddadhānaśca saṃśayātmā vinaśyati
nāyaṃ loko'sti na paro na sukhaṃ saṃśayātmanaḥ 4-40
verses.colloquial:
ajnash cha ashraddadhaanash cha samshayaatmaa vinashyati
naayam lokah asti na paro na sukham samshaya aatmanah 4-40
verses.translation_reworded: The ignorant person, without faith and full of self-doubt, goes to ruin. For the doubter there is neither this world, nor the next, nor any happiness.

verses.title: 4.41 yoga-sannyasta-karmanam
verses.sanskrit:
योगसंन्यस्तकर्माणं ज्ञानसञ्छिन्नसंशयम् ।
आत्मवन्तं न कर्माणि निबध्नन्ति धनञ्जय ॥ ४-४१॥
verses.roman:
yogasaṃnyastakarmāṇaṃ jñānasañchinnasaṃśayam
ātmavantaṃ na karmāṇi nibadhnanti dhanañjaya 4-41
verses.colloquial:
yoga samnyasta karmaanam jnaana sanchinna samshayam
aatmavantam na karmaani nibadhnanti dhananjaya 4-41
verses.translation_reworded: One who has renounced action through Yoga, whose doubts have been torn apart by Knowledge, and who is master of himself, is not bound by actions, O Dhananjaya.

verses.title: 4.42 tasmad ajnana-sambhutam
verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादज्ञानसम्भूतं हृत्स्थं ज्ञानासिनात्मनः ।
छित्त्वैनं संशयं योगमातिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भारत ॥ ४-४२॥ 

ॐ तत्सदिति श्रीमद्भगवद्गीतासूपनिषत्सु
ब्रह्मविद्यायां योगशास्त्रे श्रीकृष्णार्जुनसंवादे
ज्ञानकर्मसंन्यासयोगो नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः ॥ ४॥
verses.roman:
tasmādajñānasambhūtaṃ hṛtsthaṃ jñānāsinātmanaḥ
chittvainaṃ saṃśayaṃ yogamātiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhārata  4-42

oṃ tatsaditi śrīmadbhagavadgītāsūpaniṣatsu
brahmavidyāyāṃ yogaśāstre śrīkṛṣṇārjunasaṃvāde
jñānakarmasaṃnyāsayogo nāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ 4
verses.colloquial:
tasmaad ajnaana sambhuutam hritstham jnaanaasinaatmanah
chittva enam samshayam yogam aatishtha uttishtha bhaarata

om tatsad iti shriimad bhagavad giitaa suupanishatsu
brahma vidyaayaam yoga shaastre shrii krishna arjuna samvaade
jnaana karma samnyaasa yogo naama chaturtho'dhyaayah 4
verses.translation_reworded:
So take the sword of Knowledge and cut through this doubt about the Self, born of ignorance and lodged in your heart. Take refuge in Yoga. Stand up, O Bharata.

So ends the fourth discourse, called "The Yoga of Knowledge and Renunciation of Action," in the Upanishads of the glorious Bhagavad Gita, the science of the Eternal, the scripture of Yoga, the dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna.
